flags.note: The listing describes a 'polished 14k, 18k gold or platinum band' but does not itself use the word 'solid'; that comes from Aurate's help-centre policy.

Superseded by the P3 re-read: the live page shows $2,858 against a specific in-stock variant (14k gold, yellow, size 7), so price_type is now 'listed'. The 18k and platinum prices are still not captured.

CORRECTED by the P3 re-read: the listing publishes "Weight: 5.5-8.5g", a range spanning the 14k/18k/platinum options. No single gram figure exists for the ring a buyer receives, so weight_g stays null and nothing is estimated. Ask the seller for the weight of the exact variant in writing.

The published weight is a 3.0 g-wide range (5.5-8.5g). At $4,026.79/oz the difference between the ends is more than the entire melt value of a light band, so the range cannot be used for a price-per-gram test.

The live listing carries the notices "Exchange for size only. Final Sale!" and "Exchange only! Return & cancellation policy.", both linking to https://auratenewyork.com/pages/terms-conditions-exchange-only — while the same page displays a "Free Returns" service badge and "Lifetime Warranty". A $2,858 engagement ring that can only be exchanged for size is precisely the case the buying checklist says to walk away from unless the seller confirms otherwise in writing.

Band width: the copy says "a refined 1.8mm width" while the specs block says "Width: 2.75mm / Thickness: 1.8mm". Diamond clarity: the copy says "VVS clarity", the specs say "1 Round VS/EF Lab Grown Diamond", and a quality badge on the same page says "SI Clarity Only". All three readings are recorded; none is averaged or chosen.
No hallmark / maker's-mark statement on the listing.

products.notes: Diamond described as "EF color, VVS clarity" in the product copy, "VS/EF" in the specs block, with an "SI Clarity Only" quality badge elsewhere on the same page. products.price_recheck: 2026-10-22 (pass P3, session arena/699d8e05-gold3) — figure unchanged at $2,858.
products.weight_note: The listing DOES publish a weight, but as a range — "Weight: 5.5-8.5g" — inside a specs block that covers the 14k gold, 18k gold and platinum versions of this ring. There is no single gram figure for the ring a buyer would receive, so weight_g stays null: taking a midpoint, or the low end, would be an invented number. weight_status keeps the literal token "not published" required by scripts/verify.py, which here means "no single publishable weight", not "the page is silent". An earlier version of this record said "No ring weight in grams on the listing", which the page contradicts.

products.certification_quote: All of our engagement diamond solitaire rings come with a certificate certifying the quality (cut, color, clarity and carat) of your diamond. It is run through one of two accredited institutions: The Gemological Institute of America or The International Gemological Institute. Trust but verify, always.
products.certification_note: A certificate is promised at brand level on the product page, but the issuing lab is stated as "GIA or IGI" — which one arrives is not knowable from the page, and no report number exists before purchase. The checklist's documentation item is therefore only partly satisfiable in advance: ask which lab will issue it, in writing.
